source: Hebrew Gospel of Luke v2.1 (Van Rensburg 2026, Vat. Ebr. 100)

verses.translation: And he said to his disciples: [It is] an impossible thing [or: matter] that troubles [or: distresses] will not come, but woe to the one through whom they come

translation_notes: אמר (ואמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer (name)'. Chose H559 because the waw-prefix + narrative context indicates a verbal form 'and he said', fitting the introduction to direct speech.

דבר: Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/thing/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 because the syntax 'דבר בלתי איפשרי' reads as 'a thing impossible' — a nominal phrase, not a verb or pestilence.

אבל: Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H61 'nay/truly/yet (adversative)'. Chose H61 because the sentence structure requires an adversative conjunction ('but/yet') linking the inevitability of troubles with the woe-pronouncement.
אוי: Candidates: H188 'woe/lamentation', H189 'Evi (name)'. Chose H188 because the exclamatory 'woe to whoever' is the coherent reading in this warning context.
textual_notes: לתלמידיו — 'to his disciples' — this word (תלמידים) is post-biblical Hebrew, not attested in the standard Biblical Hebrew lexicon/Strong's. It is clearly a lamed-prefixed noun with 3ms possessive suffix meaning 'to his students/disciples'.
איפשרי — 'possible' — this is a post-biblical/medieval Hebrew form (from the root א-פ-ש-ר), not found in Strong's. Combined with בלתי it means 'impossible'.
צרות — could derive from צרה (H6869 'distress/trouble') or צר (H6862 'adversary/narrow'). The feminine plural form best fits 'troubles/distresses' (from צרה).
שבעבורו — compound relative-preposition: ש (that/who) + בעבור (on account of) + ו (him). The prefix ש is characteristic of later Hebrew as a relative particle.

verses.literal: And he said to his disciples a thing impossible it [is] that not will come troubles but woe to [the one] who on account of him they will come

verses.translation: It would be more fitting [or: worthwhile] for him that a millstone be [hung] on his neck and he be cast into the sea, than that he should do evil [or: harm] to one of the little ones

translation_notes: שוה: Candidates: H7737 'to level/equalize/be fitting', H7738 'to destroy', H7739 'to resemble (Aramaic)', H7740 'Shaveh (place)'. Chose H7737 because 'more fitting/worthwhile for him' produces a coherent comparison — drowning is preferable to causing harm to the vulnerable.

ים (בים): Candidates: H3220 'sea/large body of water', H3221 'sea (Aramaic)', H3222 'warm spring'. Chose H3220 because being cast into the sea with a millstone is the coherent physical image of drowning, fitting the warning context.

רע: Candidates: H7451 'evil/bad', H7452 'crash/noise', H7453 'associate/neighbor', H7454 'thought', H7455 'badness'. Chose H7451 because 'does evil to one of the little ones' is the coherent moral image — causing harm, consistent with the warning about bringing troubles.
אחד (לאחד): Candidates: H258 'to unify/collect thoughts', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 because 'to one of the little ones' requires a numeral/pronoun, not a verb.

מן: Candidates: H4478 'manna', H4479 'who/what', H4480 'from/out of', H4481 'from (Aramaic)', H4482 'musical chord'. Chose H4480 because the partitive 'from the little ones' (one of the little ones) is the natural construction.
שאם: The ש here functions as a comparative 'than' followed by אם 'if', yielding 'than if'. Chose H518 for אם as a conditional particle.
textual_notes: ריחים — 'millstone' — from רחה/ריחים (a millstone, dual/intensive form). Not individually listed in the provided candidates but well-attested in biblical Hebrew (cf. Deuteronomy 24:6). The ים suffix here is the dual form indicating the two stones of a mill.

ומושלך — 'and thrown/cast' — a passive participle (Hophal or similar) from שלך (H7993 'to throw/cast'). The מו- prefix and passive form indicate 'being thrown/cast'. No candidates were provided but the root is clear.
יהיה / שיהיה — forms of היה (H1961 'to be'). No candidates provided but these are standard imperfect forms of 'to be', the second prefixed with the relative ש.
הקטנים — 'the little ones' — from קטן (H6996 'small/young'). The article ה + adjective used substantively as 'the little/young ones'.

The syntax allows two readings of the comparison: (1) 'it would be more fitting for him [to have] a millstone on his neck and be thrown into the sea than if he does evil...' or (2) the שאם could introduce the condition under which the millstone punishment applies. Reading (1) is more natural as a 'better X than Y' construction.

verses.literal: More it will be fitting for him that will be a millstone on his neck and thrown into the sea than if he does evil to one from the little ones

verses.translation: And hear you if sinning sins against you your brother reprove him and he does repentance and forgive to him.

translation_notes: אם (H517 vs H518): H517 'mother' vs H518 'if/conditional'. The clause 'if your brother sins' demands the conditional. Chose H518.
חטא חטא: The doubled form (infinitive absolute + finite verb) is a standard Hebrew intensifying construction meaning 'truly sins' or 'commits a sin.' Both instances are H2398.

ומחול: The candidates H4234 'dance' and H2342 'to twist/whirl' are possible consonantal readings, but in post-biblical Hebrew the root מחל means 'to forgive.' The context 'repentance → forgive him' makes forgiveness the only coherent reading. This is a later Hebrew usage not captured in the Strong's biblical entries.
textual_notes: אתם: The Strong's candidate H864 'Etham, a place' is clearly wrong in context; this is the second person plural pronoun 'you' (אַתֶּם), which functions independently of a Strong's number in most lexicons.
ומחול: The consonants could theoretically yield 'dance' (H4234) but in context this is clearly the post-biblical Hebrew imperative 'forgive.' This word reflects later Hebrew vocabulary.

verses.literal: And hear you if sinning sins against you your brother reprove him and he does repentance and forgive to him.

verses.translation: And if seven times he sins against you and seven in a day he returns to you and says I have repented you shall forgive to him.

translation_notes: שבע (first and second): H7646 'to sate' vs H7650 'to swear' vs H7651 'seven'. The phrase 'seven times' requires the numeral. Chose H7651.
ביום (H3117 vs H3118): Both mean 'day.' H3117 is the standard Hebrew form. Chose H3117.

ישוב: The Strong's candidate H3437 'Jashub' (a proper name) shares consonants but is clearly wrong; this is the imperfect of שוב 'to return/repent' — a standard Hebrew verb not fully listed among candidates. Context demands 'he returns to you.'
textual_notes: ישוב: The only Strong's candidate given (H3437 'Jashub') is a proper name. The actual word is clearly a Qal imperfect of שׁוּב (H7725 'to return'), which was not listed among the candidates. The context 'returns to you and says I have repented' makes this certain.

verses.literal: And if seven times he sins against you and seven in a day he returns to you and says I have repented you shall forgive to him.

verses.translation: And said the sent ones teach us lord lord increase us.

translation_notes: אדון (H113 vs H114): H113 'sovereign/master' vs H114 'Addon, a person.' The vocative address 'Master, Master' fits the disciples addressing their teacher. Chose H113 for both.
textual_notes: ה<לוחים: The < symbol likely represents a damaged or unclear letter. The word is probably השלוחים 'the sent ones / the apostles' (from שלח, to send). The missing letter appears to be ש.
The doubled אדון אדון may be an emphatic vocative ('Master, Master!') or could reflect a scribal repetition. The doubling appears intentional as an intensified address.

verses.literal: And said the sent ones teach us lord lord increase us.

verses.translation: And the lord said to them if to you faithfulness like a grain of mustard and you will say to this the tree let it be cut and let it be thrown into the sea it will hear to you.

translation_notes: אמר (H559 vs H561 vs H563 etc.): H559 'to say' vs H561 'something said' vs H563 'a lamb.' The verb form 'said to them' requires H559. Chose H559.
להם: H3859 'to burn/rankle' vs ל + הם H1992 'to them.' Clearly the prepositional phrase 'to them.' Context: 'the master said to them.'
אם (H517 vs H518): Conditional 'if' is required: 'if you have faith.' Chose H518.
לזה (H2088 vs H2089 vs H2090): H2088 'this' vs H2089 'a sheep.' 'To this tree' is coherent. Chose H2088.
מושלך (H7993 vs H7994): H7993 'to throw/cast' vs H7994 'pelican.' A passive participle 'thrown/cast' into the sea makes sense. Chose H7993.
בים (H3220 vs H3222): 'Into the sea' is the natural reading for a tree being cast. Chose H3220.
textual_notes: כגרגיר and חרדל have no Strong's candidates listed — these are post-biblical or specialized terms. גרגיר means 'grain/seed' and חרדל means 'mustard' in later Hebrew.
יכרת could be parsed as Niphal imperfect of כרת 'to cut/cut off' (= be cut down/uprooted) or as a jussive 'let it be cut.' The context of a command ('say to this tree') favors the jussive reading.

verses.literal: And the lord said to them if to you faithfulness like a grain of mustard and you will say to this the tree let it be cut and let it be thrown into the sea it will hear to you.

verses.translation: Who from you there is to him a servant straying and keeping the cattle possibly will come the troubles to him the troubles that would be a millstone to the sea who that he [is] returning from the field will say immediately pass and serve.

translation_notes: עבד (H5647-H5652): H5650 'a servant' fits as the noun subject: 'a servant plowing.' Chose H5650.
שהוא (H1931 vs H1933 etc.): Relative ש + pronoun 'he' = 'that he [is].' Chose H1931.
מן (H4480 vs others): 'From the field' — partitive/source preposition. Chose H4480.
השדה (H7704 vs H7705): H7704 'a field' vs H7705 'a wife.' 'Returning from the field' is the coherent agricultural image. Chose H7704.
עבור (H5668 vs H5669): H5668 'crossed/transit' — as an imperative 'pass over/come.' Alternatively H5669 'stored grain' makes no sense as a command. Chose H5668.
textual_notes: This section appears garbled or contains a textual conflation. The text seems to combine material from the millstone saying (section 2) — 'the troubles that would be a millstone to the sea' — with the parable of the servant returning from the field. The words תבאנההצרות appear run together and the sequence 'possibly will come the troubles to him the troubles that would be a millstone to the sea' seems to be a scribal insertion or marginal gloss that interrupts the servant parable.

תועה (H8442 'error/going astray'): In context of a servant working in the field, this may be a corruption of תועה meaning 'plowing' (from תעה?) or the text may genuinely say 'an erring servant.' The parallel with agricultural imagery (field, cattle) makes 'plowing' more likely but תועה consonantally means 'straying.'
ה<ורים: The damaged letter makes this uncertain. It may be הבורים, השורים (the oxen), or another word. The agricultural context suggests cattle/oxen.
ושומעך at the end: likely ומשמשך 'and he serves you' or could be parsed as 'and your listener' — but the ש-מ-ע root in context of serving a master at table likely means 'obey/serve.'

verses.literal: Who from you there is to him a servant straying and keeping the cattle possibly will come the troubles to him the troubles that would be a millstone to the sea who that he [is] returning from the field will say immediately pass and serve.

verses.translation: And not will he say to him prepare that I eat and serve me until that I finish to eat and to drink and after you will eat and will drink.

translation_notes: לא (H3808 vs H3809): Standard Hebrew negation. Chose H3808.
עד (H5703-H5708): H5704 'until/as far as' fits: 'until I finish.' Chose H5704.
ואחר (H309-H313): H310 'after/afterward' fits: 'and afterward you eat.' Chose H310.
אתה (H857 vs H859): H857 'to arrive' vs H859 'you (singular).' 'And afterward you will eat' requires the pronoun. Chose H859.

verses.literal: And not will he say to him prepare that I eat and serve me until that I finish to eat and to drink and after you will eat and will drink.

verses.translation: And will find that servant favor in the eyes of his lord because he did his commandment I do not think.

translation_notes: עבד (H5647-H5652): H5650 'a servant' — the noun is the subject of the sentence. Chose H5650.
חן (H2580 vs H2581): H2580 'grace/favor' vs H2581 'Chen, a name.' 'Find favor in the eyes of' is a standard Hebrew idiom. Chose H2580.
כי (H3587 vs H3588): H3587 'a brand/scar' vs H3588 'because/for.' The causal conjunction makes sense: 'because he did his commandment.' Chose H3588.
textual_notes: The phrase וימצא אותו עבד חן could be parsed as 'will that servant find favor' (interrogative implied by context) or 'that servant found favor' (narrative). The following איני חושב ('I do not think so') confirms this is a rhetorical question expecting a negative answer.

verses.literal: And will find that servant favor in the eyes of his lord because he did his commandment I do not think.

verses.translation: So upon you when you have done all the things that he commanded to you you shall say we [are] servants and not profitable what was upon us to do we did.

translation_notes: כן (H3651 vs H3652 vs H3653 vs H3654): H3651 'so/thus' is the adverb connecting this conclusion to the preceding parable. Chose H3651.
כי (H3587 vs H3588): H3588 'because/when' — 'when you have done all things.' Chose H3588.
כל (H3605 vs H3606): Both mean 'all/whole.' H3605 is the standard Hebrew form. Chose H3605.
מה (H4100 vs H4101): Both are interrogative/relative 'what.' H4100 is standard Hebrew. Chose H4100.

לעשות: The candidates H6219 'polished' and H6220 'Ashvath' are not applicable. This is the infinitive construct of עשה (H6213) 'to do' with the preposition ל. The Strong's candidates provided do not match the actual word.
textual_notes: <עלינו: The < symbol indicates a damaged or unclear letter at the beginning. The word is likely שעלינו ('that [was] upon us') or simply עלינו ('upon us'). The phrase מה עלינו לעשות means 'what was incumbent upon us to do.'
The term מועילים ('profitable/useful') is a post-biblical Hebrew participle from the root יעל meaning 'to benefit/profit.' It has no Strong's entry as it is not found in the biblical text.

verses.literal: So upon you when you have done all the things that he commanded to you you shall say we [are] servants and not profitable what was upon us to do we did.

verses.translation: And it happened while Yeshua [was] walking to Jerusalem passing through the midst of Shomron and Galilah

translation_notes: בעוד (עוד): Candidates: H5749 'to duplicate/testify', H5750 'iteration/continuance (adverb: still, while)', H5751 same as H5750. Chose H5750 because with the prefix ב it forms 'while' — a temporal adverb fitting the narrative setting of an ongoing journey.
גלילה: H1552 'a circuit or region' — this is the standard Hebrew designation for the Galilee district.
textual_notes: ונעשה lacks Strong's candidates; parsed as ו + נעשה (nifal of עשה 'to be done/happen'), functioning as a narrative opener 'and it happened'.
עובר lacks Strong's candidates; parsed as a participle of עבר 'to cross/pass through'.

verses.literal: And it happened while Yeshua [was] walking to Jerusalem passing through the midst of Shomron and Galilah

verses.translation: And when he entered into a certain village came to him ten men leprous who [were] standing from afar

translation_notes: במגדול: Candidates: H4024 'Migdol, a place in Egypt', H1419 (root גדול) 'great'. The prefix ב+מ could yield 'in a large [place]' — i.e. a village/settlement. H4024 refers to a specific Egyptian locale which is geographically incoherent here (we are between Samaria and Galilee). Reading as ב + מגדול where מגדול is a variant or construct meaning 'a large [settlement]/village.' Chose contextual reading of a settlement.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 because 'one' modifies the village — 'a certain village' — standard usage.
רחוק: H7350 'remote, far off' — with prefix מ this gives 'from afar', fitting the lepers standing at a distance as required by purity laws.
textual_notes: באו lacks explicit Strong's candidates for בוא (H935 'to come/enter'); the candidate given was H176 (או 'or') which does not fit. Parsed as באו = 3mp perfect of בוא 'they came'.

במגדול is ambiguous — it could be parsed as a proper noun (Migdol) or as ב + מגדול meaning 'in a large/great [place]'. Context demands a generic settlement between Samaria and Galilee, not an Egyptian location.

verses.literal: And when he entered into a certain village came to him ten men leprous who [were] standing from afar

verses.translation: And crying out in a voice high Yeshua have compassion upon us

translation_notes: רם: The only candidate given is H7410 (Ram, a proper name), but the consonants רם also carry the adjectival meaning 'high, exalted, loud' (cf. the root רום H7311). In context, 'a high/loud voice' is the coherent reading — a proper name makes no sense modifying קול.

חמול: H2538 is listed as a proper name (Chamul). However, the root חמל means 'to have compassion/spare' (H2550). In context, lepers crying out 'have compassion upon us' is the only coherent reading — a proper name inserted mid-cry makes no sense.
textual_notes: רם: Strong's only offers H7410 (proper name Ram), but the consonants clearly function as the adjective 'high/loud' from the root רום. This is a lexicon gap, not a genuine ambiguity.
חמול: Strong's only offers H2538 (proper name Chamul), but the consonants function as an imperative from the root חמל 'to have compassion/spare' (H2550). Context demands the verbal reading.

verses.literal: And crying out in a voice high Yeshua have compassion upon us

verses.translation: And when saw-them Yeshua he said go and show-yourselves to the priests and it happened that while-they [were] walking they were changed

translation_notes: וכאשר (אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because וכאשר = 'and when' — a standard temporal conjunction introducing a narrative clause.

ראם: Candidates: H7213 'to rise', H7214 'a wild bull'. Neither fits — but the consonants ראם can also be parsed as ראה + suffix ם = 'he saw them' (from ראה H7200 with 3mp object suffix). This is the only coherent reading: 'when Yeshua saw them.'
אמר: Candidates include H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the narrative requires a speech verb introducing the command that follows.
אל: Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H413 'to/toward'. Chose H413 because 'show yourselves to the priests' requires a directional preposition.
textual_notes: ראם: The provided candidates (H7213 'to rise', H7214 'wild bull') don't match the context. The consonants are best parsed as ראה + ם (saw them), from root ראה H7200. This is a parsing issue, not a genuine ambiguity.
לכו: No Strong's candidate fits (H3551 'a window' for כו). This is clearly the imperative plural of הלך 'to go' — לכו 'go!'
נשתנו: No candidates provided. Parsed as a hitpael/nitpael of שנה 'to change' — 'they were changed/transformed', referring to their healing from leprosy.

verses.literal: And when saw-them Yeshua he said go and show-yourselves to the priests and it happened that while-they [were] walking they were changed

verses.translation: And one from them when he saw that he was changed he returned and praised YHWH in a voice great

translation_notes: אחד: H258 'to unify' vs H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 — 'and one of them' is the natural reading for an individual singled out from a group.
מהם (הם): H1990 'Ham (region)', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 — with prefix מ gives 'from them', referring to the ten lepers.
כשראה (ראה): H7200 'to see', H7201 'vulture', H7202 'seeing/experiencing', H7203 'seer/vision', H7204 'Roeh'. Chose H7200 — 'when he saw' is the natural verbal reading in this narrative clause.
שבח: H7623 'to address in a loud tone / to praise', H7624 'to adulate/adore'. Both are close in meaning. Chose H7623 because it specifically emphasizes vocal praise, matching 'with a great voice'.
textual_notes: חזר has no Strong's candidates provided. This is a post-biblical Hebrew word meaning 'to return/turn back', functionally equivalent to שוב.

verses.literal: And one from them when he saw that he was changed he returned and praised YHWH in a voice great

verses.translation: And he fell upon his face making supplication before [the] feet of Yeshua [the] Anointed and he was a Samaritan

translation_notes: נפל: H5307 'to fall', H5308 same (Aramaic), H5309 'an abortion'. Chose H5307 — 'and he fell' is the natural narrative action of prostration.
על: H5920 'the top/aloft', H5921 'upon/over', H5922 same (Aramaic), H5923 'a yoke'. Chose H5921 — 'upon his face' is a standard prostration idiom.

חנות: H2588 'a vault/prison', H2589 'supplication'. Chose H2589 — 'making supplication' before someone's feet is the coherent image of worship/thanksgiving; 'making a prison' before feet makes no sense.

משיח: H4899 'anointed/Messiah' vs שיח roots (H7878 'to ponder/converse', H7879 'utterance', H7880 'shrubbery'). Chose H4899 — 'Yeshua the Anointed One' is the only coherent title; the prefix מ is integral to the word משיח.
והוא: H1931 'he/she/it', H1933 'to be'. Chose H1931 — 'and he was' uses הוא as the emphatic pronoun with the following verb היה.
היה: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. Chose H1961 — 'he was a Samaritan' is a standard copular construction.
textual_notes: The latter portion of this section contains what appear to be scribal glosses or marginal notes: עבוד ושמעך ושמעך ושומעך תמתין המתן אשלם ואחרכך ואחרי כן ואח״כ. These look like variant readings, translation notes, or copyist annotations rather than continuous narrative text. They include repeated forms (ושמעך twice), apparent synonyms for 'wait' (תמתין / המתן), and multiple ways to express 'and after that' (ואחרכך / ואחרי כן / ואח״כ — the last being an abbreviation). I have excluded these from the main translation as they appear to be marginal apparatus, not part of the original text.
רגלי: H7273 is 'a footman (soldier)' but the consonants רגלי are naturally parsed as the construct plural of רגל 'foot' — 'feet of'. The construct form is the obvious reading here.

verses.literal: And he fell upon his face making supplication before [the] feet of Yeshua [the] Anointed and he was a Samaritan

verses.translation: And answered Yeshua and said were not you ten where are they the nine

translation_notes: וענה: H6030 'to respond/answer', H6031 'to depress/afflict', H6032 Aramaic form of respond, H6034 'Anah (name)'. Chose H6030 — 'and he answered' is the standard narrative formula for introducing speech.
ואמר: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 — paired with וענה in the standard formula 'answered and said'.
לא: H3808 'not', H3809 same (Aramaic). Chose H3808 — standard Hebrew negation particle.
אתה: H857 'to arrive', H858 same (Aramaic), H859 'you'. Chose H859 — 'where are you' or functioning as part of the question. However this may be parsed differently — see ambiguities.
ואין: H369 'non-entity/negative particle', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?'. Chose H369 — 'and there are not' expressing the absence of the other nine.
הם: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 — 'they' referring to the missing nine lepers.
textual_notes: The phrase מי אתה ואין הם התשעה is syntactically difficult. It could be parsed as: (a) 'Where are you? And there are not they, the nine?' — addressing the absent ones rhetorically; (b) 'Who [among] you — and where are they, the nine?' The flow suggests Yeshua is asking about the location of the missing nine. מי may function here as 'where' (an interrogative of location, which is unusual for מי but possible in later Hebrew). Alternative: אתה could be from H857 'to arrive' — 'who arrived? And where are they, the nine?' This remains genuinely ambiguous.

verses.literal: And answered Yeshua and said were not you ten where are they the nine

verses.translation: Not [one] was found who returned and gave praise to YHWH except this [one] from a people foreign

translation_notes: נתן: H5414 'to give', H5415 'give (Aramaic)', H5416 'Nathan (name)'. Chose H5414 — 'gave praise' is the natural verb for bestowing/offering praise.
שבח: H7623 'to praise loudly', H7624 'to adore'. Here functioning as a noun 'praise'. Chose H7623 as the nominal form of loud praise, consistent with the earlier usage in section 5.
זה: H2088 'this (demonstrative)', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — 'this one' pointing to the Samaritan as the sole returnee.
מעם (עם): H5971 'a people/nation', H5972 same (Aramaic), H5973 'with', H5974 same (Aramaic). Chose H5971 — 'from a people foreign' = from a foreign nation, identifying the Samaritan's ethnic origin.

נכר: H5234 'to scrutinize/recognize', H5235 'unexpected calamity', H5236 'foreign/foreigner/heathendom'. Chose H5236 — 'foreign' modifying 'people' gives the coherent meaning of someone from a foreign nation.
textual_notes: אלא: H414 is 'Ela, an Israelite' but the word here clearly functions as the post-biblical Hebrew conjunction 'except/but rather' (אלא). This is a later Hebrew particle not covered by the biblical Strong's lexicon.
נמצא lacks Strong's candidates; parsed as nifal perfect of מצא (H4672) 'to find' — 'was found'.

verses.literal: Not [one] was found who returned and gave praise to YHWH except this [one] from a people foreign

verses.translation: And he said to him rise and go for your faithfulness has saved you

translation_notes: אמר: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 — standard speech verb.
קום: H6965 'to rise', H6966 same (Aramaic). Chose H6965 — imperative 'rise!' as a command to the healed man.
כי: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction: for/because/that'. Chose H3588 — introduces the causal clause explaining why he should go in confidence.
textual_notes: אמונתך has no Strong's candidates provided. Parsed as אמונה (H530 'faithfulness/firmness/truth') + suffix ך 'your'. This is the standard construct for 'your faith/faithfulness'.

הושיעך has no Strong's candidates provided. Parsed as hifil perfect of ישע (H3467 'to save/deliver') + suffix ך 'you' — 'has saved you / delivered you'. The causative (hifil) stem emphasizes the effecting of deliverance.

verses.literal: And he said to him rise and go for your faithfulness has saved you

verses.translation: And [he] was asked by the Pharisees when will come [the] kingdom of God it does not come with observation

translation_notes: שאל: H7592 'to inquire/request/demand', H7593 same (Aramaic), H7594 'Sheal (name)'. Chose H7592 — 'and he was asked' (nifal) fits the passive construction where the Pharisees are asking.
מלכות: H4438 'a rule/dominion/kingdom', H3575 'Cuth (Assyrian province)'. Chose H4438 — 'kingdom of God' is the coherent reading.
האל (אל): H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H413 'to'. Chose H410 — with the article ה gives 'the God' = God, forming 'kingdom of God'.

בהעמדה (עמדה): H5979 'a station/domicile'. The root עמד means 'to stand/station/display'. With the causative prefix ה (העמדה), this becomes 'a setting up, a display, an observation post'. The reading 'with outward display/observation' fits the context of the kingdom not coming in a visibly staged manner.
textual_notes: ושאל could be parsed as active ('and he asked the Pharisees') or passive/nifal ('and he was asked by the Pharisees'). The preposition ל before פרושים supports the passive reading — 'he was asked by the Pharisees' — though ל can also indicate the indirect object. The passive reading seems more natural: the Pharisees initiated the question.

בהעמדה: The noun העמדה (from עמד) could mean 'observation/watching' (i.e. something you can observe with your eyes), 'a standing/station', or 'a setting-up/display'. All convey the idea that the kingdom does not arrive in a visually conspicuous, outwardly staged manner.

verses.literal: And [he] was asked by the Pharisees when will come [the] kingdom of God it does not come with observation

verses.translation: And not will be said here it [is] or there it [is] for behold [the] kingdom of God [is] fitting to come to you

translation_notes: הלאה (HLA'H): Candidates: H1973 'to the distance / far away', H3811 'to tire/be disgusted', H3812 'Leah'. In context of spatial contrast with הנו ('here'), H1973 'over there / far away' is the coherent counterpart.
הוא (both instances): Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1933 'to be'. Used here as emphatic pronoun 'it [is]' — standard copular usage with no verb present.
הנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold'. Following כי and introducing a declaration, H2009 'behold' fits naturally.

האל: Candidates: H408/H409 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411/H412 'these/those', H413 'to/near'. With definite article ה and following מלכות ('kingdom'), 'the God' is the only coherent reading — 'kingdom of God'.
ראוי: No Strong's candidates provided. This appears to be a later Hebrew/rabbinic form meaning 'fitting, worthy, destined' — a passive participle from a root ר-א-י.
לבא: Infinitive construct with ל of בוא (H935), 'to come'.
לכם: Preposition ל + second person masculine plural suffix, 'to you'.
textual_notes: הנו is unusual; it could be parsed as הנה + וא (a demonstrative 'behold him/it') or as הנו meaning 'here' in a locative sense. The pairing with הלאה suggests a spatial 'here' vs. 'there' contrast.
ראוי has no Strong's entry provided and appears to be post-biblical Hebrew vocabulary meaning 'fitting/worthy/destined'. Its exact nuance — 'is about to' vs. 'is fitting to' — is uncertain.

verses.literal: And not will be said here it [is] or there it [is] for behold [the] kingdom of God [is] fitting to come to you

verses.translation: And he said to his disciples will come days that you will desire to see one day of [the] son of the human and not you will see him

translation_notes: ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. Verb form with vav-consecutive clearly indicates H559 'and he said'.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify/collect thoughts', H259 'one/first'. As an adjective modifying יום, H259 'one' is the natural reading.
מבן: מ (from/of) + בן. Candidates for בן: H1121 'son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 'son'. In construct with האדם, H1121 'son' produces the phrase 'son of the human'.
האדם: Candidates: H120 'human being/mankind', H121 'Adam', H123 'Edom'. With definite article and following בן, this is the well-known construct 'the human/humanity' — H120.
שתאוו: ש (relative particle 'that') + תאוו (you will desire), from root א-ו-ה (H183, to desire/crave). No Strong's candidates were provided but the root is clear.
לתלמידיו: Post-biblical Hebrew word תלמיד (disciple/student) with ל prefix and 3ms possessive suffix. No Strong's entry exists for this rabbinic term.
textual_notes: שתאוו could theoretically be parsed as ש + תאוו from root ת-א-ו (but this is not attested); the standard reading is relative ש + imperfect of אוה 'to desire'.
מבן האדם: The מ could be partitive ('one of the days of the son of humanity') rather than possessive. Context favors 'one day of/belonging to the son of humanity'.

verses.literal: And he said to his disciples will come days that you will desire to see one day of [the] son of the human and not you will see him

verses.translation: And they will say to you behold-it to yonder he [is] not you shall desire to go and not you shall go after him

translation_notes: הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1933 'to be'. As a pronoun completing the locative clause 'over there he [is]', H1931 is correct.
להלן: This appears to be ל + הלן, a demonstrative adverb meaning 'yonder/further on' — related to הלאה (H1973). This is a post-biblical Hebrew form for 'over there'.
תחפצו: From root חפץ (H2654, to delight in / desire). Second person masculine plural imperfect, 'you shall desire'. With preceding לא this becomes a prohibition: 'do not desire'.
textual_notes: ויאמרו could be vav-consecutive perfect (past narrative 'and they said') or vav + imperfect ('and they will say'). Given the future context of the preceding section (days will come), the future reading is more coherent.

להלן is not standard biblical Hebrew; it appears to be a later Hebrew adverb meaning 'further on / yonder'. It could theoretically be parsed as ל + הלן from root לון/לין 'to lodge', but the spatial contrast with הנו makes 'yonder' far more natural.
לא תחפצו: This could be read as a prohibition ('do not desire!') or a prediction ('you will not desire'). The parallel with לא תלכו and the imperative sense of the passage suggests prohibition.

verses.literal: And they will say to you behold-it to yonder he [is] not you shall desire to go and not you shall go after him

verses.translation: For as the sun shining under the skies and causing to shine so will be [the] son of the human in his day

translation_notes: כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction: for/because/that'. As a conjunction introducing a simile, H3588 is clearly correct.
תחת: Candidates: H8478 'under/beneath', H8480 'Tachath (place name)'. In the phrase 'under the skies', H8478 is the natural spatial preposition.
כן: Candidates: H3651 'so/thus', H3653 'pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Following a כמו simile clause, H3651 'so/thus' completes the comparison naturally.
בן: Candidates: H1121 'son', H1122 'Ben (name)'. In construct with האדם, H1121 'son' is clearly intended.
האדם: H120 'human being/mankind' — same construct phrase as section 2.
שה<מש: ש (the/that) + שמש (H8121, sun). The < indicates a letter was unclear but the context of shining under the skies confirms 'sun'.
ה<מים: ה + שמים (H8064, heavens/skies). The < again marks an unclear letter. 'The heavens/skies' fits perfectly with תחת.
ומזריח: Hiphil (causative) participle of זרח (H2224, to rise/shine). 'Causing to shine / illuminating' — the sun both shines and causes illumination.
The apostrophe mark ' likely represents a word or phrase that was illegible or lost in the manuscript.
textual_notes: שה<מש and ה<מים both have unclear consonants marked with <. Context strongly supports שמש (sun) and שמים (heavens) respectively, but the physical manuscript is damaged at these points.

The ' mark between ומזריח and כן may represent a lost word or a scribal mark. It could have been an object of the illumination (e.g., 'everything') or a continuation of the description. The translation treats it as a lacuna.

ומזריח could be parsed as 'and causing to rise/shine' (Hiphil of זרח) or potentially as a different verbal form. The Hiphil causative fits the image of the sun illuminating everything beneath the sky.

verses.literal: For as the sun shining under the skies and causing to shine so will be [the] son of the human in his day

verses.translation: Surely first [it was] obligated to him to suffer multitude of things and his being rejected on behalf of the generation this

translation_notes: בעד: H1157 'in up to, over against, for, on behalf of'. In context of rejection by a generation, this functions as 'by' or 'on behalf of / on account of'.

הדור: Candidates: H1752 'to gyrate/remain', H1754 'circle/ball', H1755 'generation/age', H1756 'Dor (place)'. With definite article and demonstrative הזה, 'the generation' (H1755) is clearly intended.
הזה: The consonants הזה could be H1957 'to dream' or the demonstrative ה + זה (H2088 'this'). As a demonstrative modifying הדור, H2088 'this' is the only coherent reading.

חוייב: A passive form (Pual or similar) from root חוב/חיב, meaning 'to be obligated/liable'. This is post-biblical Hebrew vocabulary; no Strong's number directly matches. It conveys necessity or obligation.

מוזם: This appears to be a passive participle, likely from root זמם or a related form meaning 'despised/rejected'. Alternatively it could derive from a root meaning 'plotted against'. The context of suffering favors 'rejected/despised'.
ראשונה: Feminine form of ראשון (H7223), used adverbially: 'first / firstly'.
לסבול: Infinitive construct of סבל (H5445), 'to bear/carry/suffer'.
רוב: From H7230, 'multitude/abundance'.
דברים: Plural of דבר (H1697), 'words/things/matters'.
textual_notes: מוזם is difficult. It could derive from: (1) זמם 'to plan/plot' in a passive sense ('plotted against'), (2) a form related to זום/מזם meaning 'rejected/despised', or (3) a scribal variant. The context of suffering and generational rejection favors 'rejected/despised' but the exact root is uncertain.

בעד could mean 'by' (agency — rejected BY this generation) or 'on behalf of / for the sake of' (rejected FOR this generation). Both are grammatically possible; the former produces a more natural image of rejection.
חוייב has no standard Strong's entry; it is post-biblical Hebrew. The doubled yod suggests an intensive passive form conveying strong obligation.

verses.literal: Surely first [it was] obligated to him to suffer multitude of things and his being rejected on behalf of the generation this

verses.translation: And as [it] was done in [the] days of Noah so will be in [the] days of [the] son of the human

translation_notes: וכאשר: Candidates for אשר: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/that/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher'. With כ prefix and ו, this is 'and as/when' — H834 as a relative conjunction.
כן: H3651 'so/thus' — completing the comparison 'as... so...'.
בן האדם: Same construct as previous sections — H1121 'son' + H120 'the human'.
נעשה: Niphal (passive) perfect of עשה (H6213), 'was done/was made'.

verses.literal: And as [it] was done in [the] days of Noah so will be in [the] days of [the] son of the human

verses.translation: Eating and drinking taking wives and making marriages and Noah in the ark and came the flood and killed all of them

translation_notes: המבול: Candidates: H3999 'a deluge', H944 'produce', H945 'Bul (month)'. In the context of the Noah narrative, H3999 'deluge/flood' is the only coherent reading.
והרג: Candidates: H2026 'to smite with deadly intent', H2027 'slaughter'. As a verb form (vav + perfect), H2026 fits: 'and [it] killed'.
את: Candidates: H852 'portent', H853 'object marker', H854 'with/near', H855 'hoe'. Before כולם (all of them), H853 as the direct object marker is standard.
נשים: Plural of אשה (H802), 'wives/women'. Could also theoretically be from נשא but 'wives' fits the marriage context.
ועושין and נישואין: Both use the -ין plural ending typical of post-biblical/Mishnaic Hebrew rather than the biblical -ים.
בתיבה: ב + תיבה (H8392), 'in the ark'.
textual_notes: ונח בתיבה is elliptical — it seems to omit the verb. It could mean 'and Noah [was/entered] in the ark'. The narrative logic implies entry into the ark as the turning point before the flood.
The -ין endings on ועושין and נישואין mark this as post-biblical Hebrew morphology.

verses.literal: Eating and drinking taking wives and making marriages and Noah in the ark and came the flood and killed all of them

verses.translation: Also so as [it] was done in [the] days of Lot eating and drinking buying and selling planting and building

translation_notes: כן: H3651 'so/thus' — used adverbially with גם to mean 'likewise'.
לוט: Candidates: H3874 'to wrap up', H3875 'a veil', H3876 'Lot, Abraham's nephew'. In narrative context paralleling Noah, H3876 'Lot' is clearly the referent.
שנעשה: ש (relative 'that/which') + נעשה (Niphal of עשה, 'was done').

verses.literal: Also so as [it] was done in [the] days of Lot eating and drinking buying and selling planting and building

verses.translation: And in [the] day went out Lot from Sodom rained fire and sulfur from the skies and all of them destroyed

translation_notes: יצא: Candidates: H3318 'to go/bring out', H3319 same. H3318 as the standard form: 'went out'.
לוט: H3876 'Lot' — same as section 8.
אש: Candidates: H784 'fire', H786 'there is/are', H787 'foundation'. Paired with גפרית (sulfur) and the verb המטיר (rained), H784 'fire' is the only coherent reading.
מן: Candidates: H4478 'manna', H4480 'from/out of'. As a preposition before ה<מים (the heavens), H4480 'from' is clearly correct.
ה<מים: Same as section 4 — השמים (H8064), 'the heavens/skies', with a damaged consonant.
המטיר: Hiphil (causative) perfect of מטר (H4305), 'caused to rain / rained down'. The subject is implied (God).
השמיד: Hiphil of שמד (H8045), 'caused to be destroyed / annihilated'.
textual_notes: ה<מים again has a damaged consonant. Context (fire and sulfur raining from above) confirms שמים 'heavens'.
וכולם השמיד: The subject of השמיד is unstated. It could be God (implied from המטיר) or the flood of fire itself. The causative Hiphil suggests a personal agent — most likely God.

verses.literal: And in [the] day went out Lot from Sodom rained fire and sulfur from the skies and all of them destroyed

verses.translation: According to this will be in [the] day that [the] son of [a] human will be revealed
words: according to / in the manner of

translation_notes: זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Following כפי ('according to'), H2088 'this' is the clear demonstrative referent.
שבן: ש (relative 'that') + בן (H1121 'son'). 'That [the] son of...'
אדם: H120 'human being/mankind' — without definite article here, but the same construct phrase 'son of humanity' as elsewhere in this text.

מגולה: The candidate given is H1473 גולה 'exile/exiles'. However, מגולה with the מ prefix more naturally reads as a passive participle from גלה (H1540, 'to uncover/reveal'). The מ- prefix + גולה pattern yields 'revealed/uncovered/disclosed'. The dictionary entry H1473 refers to the noun 'exile', but the participial form here clearly means 'revealed'.
textual_notes: מגולה: The provided Strong's candidate H1473 means 'exile', but the form מגולה is best understood as a Pual passive participle of גלה (H1540) meaning 'revealed/uncovered'. If read as related to H1473 'exile', it would mean 'exiled/in exile', which does not fit the eschatological context of the son of humanity appearing in a day of judgment. 'Revealed' is strongly preferred.

אדם here lacks the definite article ה that appears in other sections (האדם). This could indicate a slightly different nuance — 'a human' vs. 'the human' — or simply be a scribal variation in this manuscript.

verses.literal: According to this will be in [the] day that [the] son of [a] human will be revealed

verses.translation: In that moment whoever will be on [the] roof and his vessels in [the] house not let him descend to gather them and likewise whoever will be in [the] field not let him turn back
words: who will be (relative + future of היה)
who will be (relative + future of היה)

translation_notes: שעה (שעה): Candidates: H8159 'to gaze at', H8160 'a moment/hour'. Chose H8160 because 'in that moment/hour' fits the temporal clause opening this sentence.
בבית (בית): Candidates: H1004 'house', H1005 'house (Aramaic)', H1006 'Bajith (place)', H3487 'sign of object'. Chose H1004 because the context describes possessions being inside a dwelling.
ירד: Candidates: H3381 'to descend', H3382 'Jered (proper noun)'. Chose H3381 because the rooftop context requires a verb of going down.
וכן (כן): Candidates: H3651 'so/likewise', H3652 'so (Aramaic)', H3653 'pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 because it functions as a conjunction linking two parallel warnings.

בראש (ראש): Candidates: H7217 'head (Aramaic)', H7218 'head/top/beginning', H7219 'poisonous plant', H7220 'Rosh (name)'. The consonantal text reads בראש. In the parallel tradition this word corresponds to 'field' (שדה). However, בראש literally means 'at the head/top'. This could mean 'at the head [of the field]' or 'outside/in the open.' I chose H7218 as the base reading, understanding it contextually as 'in the field' — the outdoor counterpart to the rooftop scenario. This is an ambiguity worth flagging.

ישוב: The only Strong's candidate offered is H3437 'Jashub (proper name)', but the consonants ישוב clearly parse as yiqtol 3ms of שוב (to return, H7725). The listing is incomplete; this is a verb form meaning 'let him return/turn back.'
וקנקניו: No Strong's candidates provided. The word קנקן means 'jar/vessel/pitcher' (post-biblical Hebrew). With prefix ו and pronominal suffix יו, this means 'and his jars/vessels/belongings.'
לקבצם: No Strong's candidates provided. This is ל (to) + קבץ (to gather, H6908) + ם (them suffix) = 'to gather them.'
textual_notes: בראש is problematic: literally 'at the head/top,' but the parallel structure (rooftop vs. outdoors) suggests a location like 'field.' This may reflect a Hebrew variant or abbreviation where בראש stands for a longer phrase. The parallel gospel tradition has 'in the field' (בשדה). The consonants here unambiguously read ראש, not שדה.
ישוב: The only Strong's candidate is H3437 (proper name Jashub), but morphologically this is plainly the imperfect of שוב (H7725, to return). The lexicon listing appears incomplete.
וקנקניו is a post-biblical Hebrew word not in the Strong's lexicon, meaning 'his jars/vessels.' This may indicate the text's late linguistic register.

verses.literal: In that moment whoever will be on [the] roof and his vessels in [the] house not let him descend to gather them and likewise whoever will be in [the] field not let him turn back

verses.translation: Remember from [the] wife of Lot
words: from the wife of (מ + אשת, construct of אשה H802)

translation_notes: לוט: Candidates: H3874 'to wrap up', H3875 'a veil', H3876 'Lot, Abraham's nephew'. Chose H3876 because 'wife of Lot' is a coherent reference to the biblical narrative of Lot's wife who turned back — directly relevant to the preceding warning about not turning backward.
זכרו: No candidates listed. The consonants זכר + ו parse as imperative masculine plural of זכר (to remember, H2142).
מאשת: No candidates listed. This is מ (from) + אשת (wife of, construct form of אשה H802).
textual_notes: The preposition מ (from) in מאשת is slightly unusual — 'remember from the wife of Lot' rather than 'remember the wife of Lot.' This may carry the nuance of 'take a lesson from' or 'remember [what happened] concerning the wife of Lot.'

verses.literal: Remember from [the] wife of Lot

verses.translation: And whoever will desire that his soul be saved will lose it and whoever whoever will lose it truly will [preserve] it
words: who will desire (ש + ירצה from רצה H7521)
that she be saved (ש + תושע from ישע H3467)

translation_notes: שירצה: Relative particle ש + imperfect of רצה (H7521, to desire/be pleased). 'Who will desire/wish.'
שתושע: Relative particle ש + hophal/nifal imperfect of ישע (H3467, to save/deliver). The ת prefix suggests 3fs — agreeing with נפש (feminine). 'That his soul be saved/delivered.'
נפשו: נפש (H5315, soul/life/self) + 3ms possessive suffix. 'His soul/life.'
יאבד: From אבד (H6, to perish/lose/destroy). In qal: 'will perish'; in piel: 'will lose/destroy.' Context suggests causative sense: 'will lose it.'

אמת (H571): 'truth/stability/faithfulness.' Used adverbially here: 'truly' or 'in truth.' This word appears where one might expect a verb like 'will save/preserve,' raising the question of whether the text is corrupt or whether אמת functions as a compressed predicate.
textual_notes: The doubled ומי ומי is unusual. This may be a scribal dittography (accidental repetition) or an emphatic construction ('and whoever, whoever...').

The final clause 'אמת אותה' is syntactically difficult. Literally: 'truly it' or 'truth it.' A verb seems to be missing. Possible explanations: (1) a verb like יחיה ('will preserve/vivify') has dropped out before or after אמת; (2) אמת functions verbally ('will make firm/establish it'); (3) the text is corrupt at this point. The parallel saying in the tradition typically ends 'will preserve/save it.' I have translated אמת adverbially and supplied the understood verb in brackets.
יאבד could be qal ('will perish') or piel ('will lose/destroy'). Since it takes a direct object (אותה), it must be piel/causative: 'will lose it.'

verses.literal: And whoever will desire that his soul be saved will lose it and whoever whoever will lose it truly will [preserve] it

verses.translation: I say to you that that the night will be two in bed one

translation_notes: אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because 'I say to you' is a natural speech formula; a ship makes no sense here.

אומר: The only candidate listed is H201 'Omar (proper name).' However, the consonants אומר clearly represent the qal active participle of אמר (H559, to say). The listing is incomplete; this is 'saying/say.'

במטה: Candidates: H4294 'branch/rod/tribe', H4295 'downward/below', H4296 'bed/couch/bier', H4297 'distortion/iniquity', H4298 'expansion'. Chose H4296 because 'two in one bed' at night produces a coherent domestic image — two people sleeping together — whereas 'two in one rod/tribe' or 'two below' would be forced in this nighttime context.
אחת: Feminine form of אחד (one, H259). Agrees with מטה (feminine noun): 'one bed.'

verses.literal: I say to you that that the night will be two in bed one

verses.translation: And [they are] answering and saying to him where will [the] lord be and he said to them in what place the body will be there will gather the messengers [ ] and they said to him that Yeshua of Nazareth [is] passing in that place

translation_notes: אנה: Candidates: H578 'to groan', H579 'to approach/meet'. However, in context this reads as the interrogative adverb אנה 'where?' (not listed among Strong's candidates but the consonants א-נ-ה support it). The blind man is asking 'where will the lord be?' which makes narrative sense. H578 'groan' and H579 'approach' do not fit an interrogative context.
אדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/controller', H114 'Addon (proper name)'. Chose H113 because the blind man is asking about the whereabouts of a lord/master figure.
להם: The prefix ל + consonants ה-מ. Candidates include H3859 'to rankle' and H1992 'them'. Chose H1992 because 'he said to them' is the natural reading in dialogue context.

שם: Candidates: H8033 'there', H8034 'name', H8035 'Shem', H8036 'name'. Chose H8033 'there' because 'there will gather the messengers' fits the locative sense of the sentence about a place where the body is.

הגוף: H1479 is the only candidate, glossed as 'to hollow/arch/close/shut'. However, the consonants ג-ו-ף in later Hebrew clearly mean 'body'. The article ה makes this a noun 'the body'. This fits the context of a proverb about where the body is, there gather the messengers.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction that/because'. Chose H3588 because 'they said to him that Yeshua...' requires a conjunction.
די: Candidates: H1767 'enough', H1768 'that/of (relative)'. Chose H1768 because 'Yeshua of Nazareth' uses the Aramaic/late Hebrew relative particle to indicate origin.
textual_notes: אנה could be the interrogative 'where?' or one of the provided candidates (H578 'groan', H579 'approach'). The interrogative reading is most natural in context but is not among the Strong's candidates provided.

The section contains a mysterious saying about 'wherever the body will be, there the messengers will gather' which appears as a displaced logion. The brackets [ ] in the text suggest a lacuna or editorial note.
הגוף: The sole Strong's candidate H1479 means 'to close/shut', but the consonants ג-ו-ף in post-biblical Hebrew clearly mean 'body'. The text likely uses the later Hebrew sense.

verses.literal: And [they are] answering and saying to him where will [the] lord be and he said to them in what place the body will be there will gather the messengers [ ] and they said to him that Yeshua of Nazareth [is] passing in that place
